subject: maths
topic: Euclidean geometry: angles, triangles and polygons (describe figures fully in words)

kept.q: In triangle ABC, AB = AC (the triangle is isosceles with AB and AC as the two equal sides). If angle BAC (the angle between the two equal sides) is 48°, find angle ABC.
kept.explanation: Since AB = AC, the base angles ABC and ACB are equal. The three angles sum to 180°, so each base angle = (180 - 48)/2 = 66°.
kept.pidgin: Since AB = AC, the two base angles (ABC and ACB) go dey equal. All three angles must add to 180°, so each base angle = (180 - 48)/2 = 66°.

kept.q: A regular polygon has 9 sides. Calculate the total number of diagonals that can be drawn inside the polygon.
kept.explanation: The number of diagonals of a polygon with n sides is given by n(n-3)/2. For n = 9, this gives 9(9-3)/2 = 9x6/2 = 27.
kept.pidgin: The formula for diagonals na n(n-3)/2. If n = 9, e go be 9(9-3)/2 = 9x6/2 = 27.

kept.q: A convex hexagon (6-sided polygon) has its 6 exterior angles forming an arithmetic progression, increasing by 10° from one angle to the next around the polygon. If the smallest exterior angle is 35°, find the largest exterior angle.
kept.explanation: The exterior angles form an AP: 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 85 (6 terms, common difference 10). Checking the sum: 35+45+55+65+75+85 = 360, which agrees with the rule that exterior angles of any convex polygon sum to 360°. The largest angle is 85°.
kept.pidgin: The exterior angles be AP: 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 85 (6 terms, common difference 10). If you add them, e go give 360°, wey match the rule say exterior angles of any convex polygon must sum to 360°. So the biggest angle na 85°.

kept.q: In triangle LMN, angle LMN = 72° and angle LNM = 54°. The bisector of angle MLN meets side MN at point K, splitting angle MLN into two equal parts. Find the size of angle MLK.
kept.explanation: First find angle MLN: 180 - 72 - 54 = 54°. Since LK bisects this angle, angle MLK = 54/2 = 27°.
kept.pidgin: First calculate angle MLN: 180 - 72 - 54 = 54°. Since LK dey cut the angle into two equal parts, angle MLK = 54/2 = 27°.
